questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Continuing to improve my language skills by being surrounded by the language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Would have been a 10 if not for how stressful it was with the classes I ended up with.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received help from my friend in figuring out how exactly to apply for classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I didn't go to orientation because I didn't have time so I wouldn't know. However, the people I went to for help were nice and helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: AirBnB. It wasn't difficult because I looked for housing several months before I went.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was stressful and somewhat difficult. It's difficult because you have to look under each department for the classes on the websystem.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You use a website and you can save the classes you want under wishes before the registration day. However, it goes so quickly because there are limited spots, so I personally had to look under each department to see what classes still had spots left because all my wished ones were taken immediately.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could call in because I couldn't log in and someone could register a class for me in the office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only got one class I wanted because all the spots were taken immediately and there are a limited amount of spots for exchange students in the ones I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to have good wifi and have a wishlist ready with many options. Also have a list of classes not on the wishlist and make sure to know what department they fall under.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My courses were fine, some were harder than others but I also took classes I have no knowledge in because I couldn't get other classes I wanted.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of listening and many of my teachers wanted active participation in the class. There were also presentations in 3 / 5 of my classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Investment Law
FTA & Law
Koreatown and Korean Wave 2
Intensive Study on British and American Novels
Content of Korean Studies and Visual Application

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Koreatown and Korean Wave 2 - the teacher was so sweet and very helpful. I learned a lot and the classes were interesting.
Intensive Study on British and American Novels - great class, read some sci fi interesting books and we dived deep into them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't join any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were different clubs, school festival with music, and other school activities. School jackets could also be bought.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: School festival

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around the country.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not a problem, but I've been there before so I can't really pinpoint anything.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and seek people out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open Koreans are about their culture and loving to let people learn.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Learn about the culture
- Prepare a good list of possible classes to take
- Travel around the country, don't just stay in the capital

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just the overall experience. Getting to go and having a good time with my friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to take some classes I didn't want and midterm week is stressful. So is the final exam week.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
